newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: SIA disappointed over Boeing 747 plans.
newsitem.headline: SIA disappointed over Boeing 747 plans.

text.p: Singapore Airlines said on Wednesday it was disappointed with Boeing Co's decision to scrap plans for a stretch version of its 747 jumbo jet.

"We are naturally disappointed with Boeing's decision to shelve plans to build the larger capacity versions of the B747 jumbo jets," Karmjit Singh, assistant director of corporate affairs, said in a statement.
He said that SIA definitely needed some of the "super jumbos", particularly at congested, slot-constrained international gateways.
"We hope that when there is sufficient market demand, Boeing will reconsider its development plans," Singh said, adding that otherwise European rival Airbus Industrie may fill the vacuum.
Boeing said on Monday it would scale back its 747-X programme as market conditions did not justify a larger version of the jumbo, estimated at more than US$7 billion.
The decision marks an end to more than three years of research that included a joint study by Boeing and partner companies in Airbus.
Boeing said it would put more resources in the near term into developing new versions of the smaller widebodies, the 767 and 777, to meet rising demand for long-range, medium-sized planes.
